about: CQS Orbital Fleet parts kit: small hull components, each designed once with fal (nano-banana-pro, then /edit with the door concept as the style reference), reconstructed on its own with Tripo H3.1 image-to-3D and normalised to true metres, so every ship composed from them shares the same door, window and rail sizes.
frame: Metres. +Z = out of the hull (surface normal), +Y = up along the part height, +X = along the width. Parts with mount.normal "+Z" have their back (mounting) face at z = 0, centred on x/y (ladder: foot at y = 0). Parts with mount.normal "+Y" (rail, antenna, container) stand on their foot/base at y = 0, centred on x/z: orient their +Y along the hull normal.
paint: Light off-white weathered paint with dark blue-grey glass, as generated; the runtime livery (src/lib/livery.js applyLivery) repaints it dark matte grey and turns the glass texels into glossy glass.
pipeline: tripo GLB -> flatten, rotate (normaliseRot, degrees, R = Rz*Ry*Rx), scale to size (per-axis where the table fixes all three dims), anchor -> dedup, prune, weld -> WebP textures (512 or 1024) -> meshopt (tools: scratchpad v7/parts/normalize.mjs, same steps as tools/optimize-glb.mjs).
sizeSource: Target sizes from the v7 parts brief; size[] is the final bbox [w, h, d].

cost.meshUsdEachNote: Tripo H3.1 price as recorded in the README (fal bills Tripo in credits)

door.notes: Crew door: 1.0 x 2.0 m hinged leaf (hinges on the -X side, grab handle and lever on +X, small viewport at eye height) recessed in a 1.4 x 2.4 x 0.3 m chamfered frame. Frame back at z = 0, front face at z = 0.3; to sit ~0.1 m proud as specified, sink it 0.2 m into the hull (position.z = -0.2 along the normal). The reconstruction mirrored the door onto the back face (hidden when mounted). Depth squashed ~0.45x relative to width to reach 0.3 m.

port.notes: Single 1.0 x 1.0 m round-cornered window aperture in a thick 1.3 x 1.3 x 0.3 m chamfered, bolted frame (frame is crisp). Back at z = 0; sink 0.2 m into the hull for the ~0.1 m proud look. KNOWN ISSUE: both reconstructions (transparent and opaque-glass concepts) left the glazing out, so the aperture is open through the part; mounted flush, the hull behind it shows through. Back it with a dark glass material at composition time or regenerate the port (e.g. H3.1 multiview) in a later round.

cargoHatch.notes: Framed 6 x 4 m double-leaf cargo hatch (hinge blocks along the top, locking bolts on the centre seam), 0.4 m deep, back at z = 0.

rail.notes: Handrail segment, 1.0 m long (X) x 1.1 m high (Y): two posts on bolted foot plates, top rail and mid rail. Mounts by its feet: origin at the centre of the foot line, feet at y = 0, the deck normal is +Y (place with +Y along the hull normal and X along the run). Tile end to end at a 1.0 m pitch (bbox includes the top-rail overhangs; posts at about x = +-0.33). Tubes read ~80-90 mm, thicker than the 50 mm spec. Reconstruction was skewed 17.5 deg in plan and was straightened.

ladder.notes: Wall rung ladder 0.5 m wide x 3.0 m tall, 11 rungs (~0.28 m pitch), standoff brackets at top and bottom. Origin at the bottom centre of the back (bracket) face: foot at y = 0, back at z = 0, +Z out of the hull. The concept was drawn ~1:3.3, so Y is stretched ~3x relative to X; rungs read slightly oval.

fal.params: texture, pbr, texture_quality detailed, geometry_quality detailed

rcs.notes: RCS quad: 1.0 x 1.0 m back plate at z = 0, chamfered block, four nozzles pointing +Y, -Y, +X, -X (nozzle exits roughly 0.35 m out from the part centre along each axis, at z ~0.3).

antenna.notes: Mast 6.0 m tall (Y) on a 0.3 m square base box, three dipole pairs (0.43 m span) and a tip. Mounts by its base: origin at the base centre, base at y = 0, the hull normal is +Y. X/Z were scaled 0.375x relative to Y so the base is 0.3 m.

dome.notes: Sensor radome ~2.46 m diameter (near-spherical, with a seam band) on a short bolted octagonal ring; flange 2.5 m at z = 0, top at z = 2.36. Axis is +Z (hull normal).

floodlight.notes: Floodlight: 0.6 m lamp housing on a U yoke, base plate at z = 0 on the hull, lamp centre ~0.4 m out. The lens aims +Y (along the hull); rotate about Z to aim it. Lens texel is blue-grey glass (livery glass); add a SpotLight at the lens centre if it should throw light.

turret.notes: Twin-barrel gun turret, ONE design: round bolted barbette ring (8 m at M), faceted gunhouse (~8.4 x 10 m, roof 6.0 m, blister top 7.0 m), flat mantlet at z = 4.06 with two embrasures, twin barrels (0.9 m OD, axes x = +-1.28, y = 4.3) protruding 6.5 m to z = 10.57, boxy sighting blister with a dark slit at the rear left of the roof. Size variants are uniform scalings (S 0.5, M 1, L 1.75). The generated barrels are shorter than the brief at every size (barrels out 3.25 / 6.5 / 11.4 m vs 6 / 14 / 24 m), so the barrels are also a separate part (twinBarrel) to be lengthened in Blender. Side access door: Tripo mirrored it onto BOTH sides (x = +-4.2, centred ~z -1.6, y ~4.0); its frame is ~2.1 x 3.3 m at M (leaf ~1.7 x 2.9), not 1 x 2 m: at M overlay the kit door.glb (1.4 x 2.4 frame fits inside the recess) or keep it as a large hatch; at S it becomes 1.05 x 1.65 m (close to a crew door) and at L 3.7 x 5.8 m (drop it or read it as a cargo hatch).

scale.key: barrel centre spacing = 2.54 m (matches turret M embrasures); overall length 11.3 m

fal.role: concept; references: the turret concept as the design reference and the door concept as the style reference

fal.params: texture, pbr, texture_quality detailed, geometry_quality detailed

twinBarrel.notes: Twin gun barrels on a 4.72 x 1.95 x 2.47 m breech block, same barrel spacing (2.54 m) and OD (0.94 m) as the turret, so it drops into the turret embrasures at the same variant scale. Back of the breech block at z = 0, barrels along +Z, barrel axes at y = 0. To fit on the turret (M): delete the turret barrels, place the breech face at the mantlet (z = 4.06 - 2.47 = 1.59) with the axes at y = 4.3; the barrels then end at z = 12.9. To reach the brief lengths, stretch the plain uniform tube section (z 6.6-10.3 at M) along Z: +5.2 m at M (14 m out), +1.6 m at S (6 m), +8.6 m at L (24 m).

railgunSegment.notes: Tileable spinal railgun section: gunmetal rails top and bottom, ceramic insulator stacks, three clamping collars / capacitor bands, cable trays on both sides, bolted end flanges. Tripo made it 4:1, not 2:1, so at the 5 m cross-section it is 19.46 m long (two brief lengths; the brief 10 m pitch would need a Blender cut). The end flanges do not match: -Z end 4.4 x 3.2 m (y 0.79-3.96), +Z end 3.3 x 3.2 m, and small rail stubs/feet stick past them; square both ends to one flange profile in Blender before tiling. The end plates are closed (flat caps), so the joints are opaque.

Tripo mirrored the door onto the back face (hidden when mounted), so the part is 1.26 m deep; sink it ~0.9 m into the hull (position.z = -0.9) so only the front ~0.35 m stands proud.

engine.interior: nearly cylindrical bell wall (r 1.0 -> 0.86) down to a flat annular floor at depth 1.225 (r 0.86-0.5); from the floor a central collar rises to depth ~0.78 (r ~0.23-0.32) with a bore of r ~0.17-0.2 that ends on the throat plate at depth 1.437. The wall list stops at the floor; the collar cannot be expressed in a monotonic profile.

bell.notes: Drive bell: dark heat-stained bell with reinforcing bands, gimbal ring, off-white combustion chamber and mounting flange, four gimbal actuators. Exit plane at z = 0, axis -Z; overall length 8.3 m at r 2.2 (3.77 exit radii). The mouth is open (Tripo did not cap it). A stray blob hangs under the bell at the exit (y down to -2.84, outside the lip): delete it in Blender. The interior is a cylinder + flat floor + raised throat collar, not a converging nozzle: for a real bell, delete the floor/collar and loft the wall to the throat.

parts2.about: Weapons, engines and large components added by the second kit pass (same pipeline: nano-banana-pro/edit with the door concept as the style reference, Tripo H3.1 image-to-3D, normalize2.mjs).
parts2.scaling: UNIFORM scaling only: one factor per part, chosen from the key dimension in scale.key; size[] is the true resulting bbox, which may differ from the brief on the other axes (noted per part).
parts2.mounts: back = +Z mount normal as in frame; foot = stands at y = 0 centred on its base/barbette axis (not the bbox), normal +Y; seg = railgun section centred on z, bottom y = 0; join = joining face at z = 0, extends +Z; front = hull-side face at z = 0, body extends to -Z; exit = bell exit-plane centre at the origin, axis -Z.
parts2.pipeline: tripo GLB -> flatten, rotate (normaliseRot, R = Rz*Ry*Rx), uniform scale to the key dimension, anchor -> dedup, prune, weld -> WebP 1024 -> meshopt (scratchpad v7/parts2/normalize2.mjs).
